sections.section_title: Theorem 4: Two diagonals of a rectangle are equal and bisect each other.
sections.content_markdown:
Proposition: Let the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of the rectangle $ABCD$ intersect at $O$. It is required to prove that,
(i) $AC = BD$
(ii) $AO = CO, BO = DO$.

Proof: | Steps | Justification | | :--- | :--- | | (1) A rectangle is also a parallelogram. Therefore, $AO = CO, BO = DO$. | [Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other] | | (2) Now between $\Delta ABD$ and $\Delta ACD$, $AB = DC$ and $AD = AD$. $\angle DAB = \angle ADC$ Therefore, $\Delta ABD \cong \Delta ACD$. Therefore, $AC = BD$ (Proved) | [ Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal ]
[ each angle is a right angle]
[ ASA theorem] |
